reviews.review:
I really enjoyed this game. It flows phenomenally on my PC. It is one of the most underrated and forgotten games in my opinion. 

Storywise, it was a strong Warhammer campaign. I really liked Titus and the other Ultramarines, as well as Lt Mira.

Really simplistic third person shooter, seems like it wants to copy the Gears of War formula but it doesn't have the mechanics or the physics engine to make it it's equal, always felt Havok was inferior to UE4 although UE4 has it's flaws.

 Played the game on hard, and while it was challenging, I felt the main mechanic of Fury mode and armor wasn't fleshed out enough to keep up with the higher damage the basic enemies were doing, like some of the elite enemies weren't as much of a problem because they didn't have any ranged attacks, guns were the name of the game even though melee seems to be what the developers wanted, when you're forced to use the Thunder Hammer it locks you out of your best guns.

The enemies used a variety of tactics, they didn't seem homogenous, although the final boss was a quick time event that really disappointed me :(. The weapons were varied although some were better than others, such as the lascannon. Graphics look really dated even for 2011, like an early 360 game, The art style is typical of warhammer 40k which tonka trucks in human form, really blocky and angular.

All in all it seems like it was a product of it's time with the sequel recreating it's story beats but doing it in a better way with more weapons and better graphics.
expected nothing, but this was a really fun game to relax to

As a little kid, I loved playing the Warhammer tabletop, those battles with my older brother were a highlight of my childhood. Space Marine is my first dive into the video game side of things, and to be completely honest, I didn't know much about the 40K lore going in, just the basics, but I was excited to learn more.

After starting the game, I got so caught up in the universe that for the next three nights, I ended up falling asleep to lore videos. I was fascinated by the depth of it all, like the 20+ organ transplants and augments that create the Ultramarines, or the wild process behind building a Dreadnought and how they're basically these venerated unstoppable war machines.

I had a great time playing through it, I was smiling for probably 95% of the campaign. The combat feels solid and satisfying, with each weapon having a good weight to it, whether you're hacking away with a chainsword or firing a bolter.

The game looks fantastic, and the maps and world design really capture the 40K feel, from massive gothic structures to chaotic battlefields. The story drew me in, and I took my time with it, one thing I really loved is how each mission flows seamlessly into the next without any loading breaks or stops, it keeps the momentum going and feels incredible. That said, I still wished it was longer because I was left wanting more when it ended (and yeah, that seamless flow probably made it feel even shorter overall).

That said, to be honest, there were a few downsides. The controls can feel a bit outdated and clunky in spots, though it's not a huge issue. I also would've liked more variety in the enemies across the different factions, it got a little repetitive fighting similar groups. The final boss fight was cinematic and made me feel powerful, but it mostly came down to a straightforward quick-time event, and I wished for more actual in-game combat to make it more engaging.

I personally only paid about $9-10 for it, and at that price, it was a fantastic experience, though I get why folks might hesitate at the full $39.99 given the length.

Overall, I'd give it a solid 8.5/10 – it's a strong entry point for someone new to 40K games like me, and it got me even more interested in the lore. I haven't tried the multiplayer yet, but I'm looking forward to checking it out soon. If you're into action games or curious about Warhammer, it's definitely worth picking up.
